claims.claim: Ordered-bipartition criterion: a bipartite n-vertex tree with classes A={x1,...,xa} and B={y1,...,yb} has a bipartition-separated graceful labeling if and only if the two classes can be ordered so that the endpoint-rank sums i+j over edges xiyj are pairwise distinct.
claims.evidence: There are n−1 edges and every rank sum lies in the n−1-element set {2,...,n}; distinctness therefore makes the sums exactly that set. Labeling xi by i and yj by n+1−j uses exactly {1,...,n}, separates the classes, and gives edge difference n+1−i−j, hence exactly {1,...,n−1}. Conversely, in any separated labeling the lower class receives the initial interval of labels. Ordering it increasingly and the upper class decreasingly expresses every edge difference as n+1 minus its endpoint-rank sum, so distinct differences imply distinct sums. The argument also covers either choice of the lower class.
claims.search_method: Direct bidirectional proof; no finite search.

claims.claim: For every caterpillar, the bipartition orders described in the final writeup give endpoint-rank sums 2,3,...,n in succession.
claims.evidence: Let ti=|Li|. Immediately before the Li block, the numbers of earlier entries in the two orders sum to Σh<i(th+1), exactly the number of previously listed leaf and spine edges. For odd i, vi has the next A-rank and the leaves have consecutive B-ranks; for even i the roles reverse. Thus the Li edges receive the next ti sums. The following spine vertex is the next entry in the opposite order, so vivi+1 receives the next sum. Induction starts at 2 and, across n−1 edges, ends at n. Empty blocks and the one-vertex case are harmless.
claims.search_method: Exact prefix-rank induction for arbitrary leaf-block sizes.

claims.evidence: Claim 1 supplies orders with all endpoint-rank sums distinct, and claim 0 converts them into the explicit graceful labeling xi↦i, yj↦n+1−j. K1 and K2 also satisfy the definition directly.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the proved criterion and explicit caterpillar orders.

claims.claim: Extreme-vertex leaf-extension lemma: if a graceful n-vertex tree has a vertex v labeled 1, attaching any s≥0 new leaves at v preserves gracefulness.
claims.evidence: Keep all old labels and assign the new leaves n+1,...,n+s. Old differences are exactly 1,...,n−1, while the new incident differences from label 1 are n,...,n+s−1. Their disjoint union is exactly the required difference set for the enlarged tree; s=0 is immediate.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic construction for arbitrary n and s.
claims.witness: New leaf with label n+j has difference n+j−1 from v, for 1≤j≤s.

claims.claim: For every r≥0, the tree obtained from the once-subdivided K1,3 by adjoining r additional leaves to its center is a graceful non-caterpillar.
claims.evidence: With center c=1 and arm pairs (ui,wi)=(7,3),(6,5),(4,2), the six differences are {6,4,5,1,3,2}={1,...,6}. Assigning the r new center-leaves labels 8,...,7+r adds differences 7,...,6+r, giving every required difference exactly once. The non-leaves c,u1,u2,u3 induce K1,3, not a path, for every r, so the tree is not a caterpillar.
claims.search_method: Direct parametric labeling and induced-nonleaf-subtree calculation.

claims.claim: The once-subdivided K1,3 has no bipartition-separated graceful labeling; hence not every tree admits the stronger alpha-type labeling used for caterpillars.
claims.evidence: After complementation, assume A={c,w1,w2,w3} is lower. If c has rank r, its three edge sums are r+1,r+2,r+3. For r=1 or 4, forcing the extreme missing sum consumes ranks (4,3) or (1,1), making the next required sum impossible. For r=2 or 3, sums 2 and 7 force both extreme pairs and the remaining ranks give 5 instead of 6, or 4 instead of 3. The checker independently enumerated all 4!*3!=144 order pairs and found none with six distinct sums, while validating the displayed graceful labeling.
claims.search_method: Four-case rank proof plus exhaustive exact enumeration of all 144 bipartition-order pairs.
claims.witness: Seven-vertex tree with edges c-ui and ui-wi for i=1,2,3; checker output: separated_orders_tested=144, separated_order_found=no.

claims.claim: The checker’s inductive generator contains exactly one representative of every unlabeled tree at each tested order.
claims.evidence: Completeness follows by deleting a leaf from any larger tree and applying induction, then reattaching it at the corresponding vertex of the representative. The rooted sorted-child code is equivalent to rooted isomorphism by induction on subtree size; rooting at the unique center, or using the unordered pair of component codes at a central edge, is therefore a complete unrooted invariant. Exact string keys eliminate collisions and retain one representative per invariant. The implementation rechecked every stored tree and code, and an independent all-Prüfer-sequence enumeration produced identical code sets through order 8.
claims.search_method: Inductive leaf attachment with exact AHU-style canonical strings; exhaustive Prüfer cross-check through n=8.

claims.claim: For n≥2, in searching for a graceful labeling, it is complete to guess an edge, give its endpoints labels 0 and n−1 in one orientation, and search the remaining labels.
claims.evidence: A graceful n-vertex tree has n−1 distinct positive differences drawn from {1,...,n−1}, so it must use n−1. Only labels 0 and n−1 realize that difference, hence they lie on an edge. Complementing every label by x↦n−1−x preserves all differences and reverses the two endpoint labels, so one fixed orientation per guessed edge is complete. The checker implements exactly this seeding.
claims.search_method: Extremal-difference proof, implemented by exhaustive edge seeding.

claims.claim: The singleton tree K1 is graceful under its unique 0-based labeling, despite having no edge.
claims.evidence: The map from the sole vertex to 0 is a bijection onto {0}; its empty edge-difference collection is pairwise distinct and equals the required empty set. The checker handles and validates this case before extreme-edge seeding.
claims.witness: K1 with its only vertex labeled 0.

claims.claim: The persisted backtracking and validation procedure is exact: every reported witness is graceful, and its pruning rules cannot remove a possible completion.
claims.evidence: The assigned vertices always induce a connected subtree, so every unassigned boundary vertex has exactly one assigned neighbor. The recursion selects a boundary vertex and exhausts every free label producing an unused parent-edge difference. A boundary vertex with no candidate cannot be completed. The additional matching prune is also necessary: any completion gives an injective matching from unresolved edges to unused differences within the checker's deliberately overapproximated domains. Thus failure of such a matching rules out completion. At a leaf of the search, the validator independently requires sorted labels 0,...,n−1 and sorted edge differences 1,...,n−1, establishing soundness.
claims.search_method: Line-by-line invariant and pruning audit, followed by 103,704,153 exact backtracking nodes in the completed run.

claims.claim: Any counterexample to the graceful tree conjecture must have at least 16 vertices and contain a vertex adjacent to at least three non-leaf vertices.
claims.evidence: The exhaustive certification excludes all orders at most 15, while the caterpillar theorem excludes every caterpillar. In any tree, the non-leaf vertices induce a connected subtree: each internal vertex on a path between two non-leaves has at least its two path neighbors. If every vertex had at most two non-leaf neighbors, this induced subtree would have maximum degree at most two and hence be a path, making the original tree a caterpillar. Contraposition gives the required vertex in any counterexample.
claims.search_method: Combination of the exact order-15 certification with a direct structural contrapositive.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof that every finite tree is graceful or one explicit finite nongraceful tree together with a rigorous nonexistence proof. The draft establishes neither: its seven-vertex example is explicitly graceful and only obstructs the stronger bipartition-separated condition, while its exhaustive result stops at 15 vertices. It nevertheless establishes correct, material progress—every caterpillar, an infinite graceful non-caterpillar family, every tree through order 15, and a necessary structural condition on any counterexample. Therefore the target verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and its final writeup expressly disclaims full resolution, so that claimed resolution is ACCURATE.
